source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: One irrelevant sentence added to grade-school math problems cuts accuracy sharply in code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003 across CoT, least-to-most, zero-shot CoT and program prompting.
numbers: Of base problems solved by greedy decoding, no more than 18% were solved for all distractor types. Macro accuracy (problem solved under every distractor) was low: e.g. code-davinci-002 COT macro 8.3 on 2-step problems vs micro 72.4 overall. text-davinci-003 COT base accuracy 80.0.
limits: 2022-23 models; 100 GSM8K base problems; one sentence only; no load manipulation.
agent_relevance: S1 intrusion is real: one off-task sentence lowers answer reliability. Treat extra context as a cost, not a neutral extra.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC) - similarity breakdown
finding: What distracts is similarity to the task, not number size. In-topic and role-name-overlapping sentences hurt most.
numbers: code-davinci-002 COT micro: in-topic 63.1 vs off-topic 80.7; role overlap yes 68.3 vs no 76.6; macro in-topic 10.2 vs off-topic 33.0. Number inside vs outside problem range: micro 70.2 vs 74.6 (small gap). text-davinci-003 with role overlap: macro 0 on problems with more than 2 steps.
limits: Same benchmark; templates hand-written. Fits relevance-similarity accounts more than load theory.
agent_relevance: Task-like distractors are the dangerous class. Test lessons or examples that resemble the problem as a distractor.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC) - mitigations
finding: Self-consistency, exemplars that contain distractors, and an 'ignore irrelevant information' instruction each help; none removes the effect.
numbers: Self-consistency with 20 samples: correct answer present in at least one sample 99.7% of the time. COT micro 72.4 -> 77.8 with the instruction; 72.4 -> 76.8 with distractor exemplars; COT+SC micro 88.1.
limits: The 99.7% is an oracle recall (any of 20), so a selector is still needed.
agent_relevance: Supports code-side voting plus an explicit filter step; instruction alone leaves most problems unstable.

source: Weston & Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention (is something you might need too)
finding: Two-pass scaffold: first regenerate the context keeping only relevant, unbiased text, then answer from the regenerated text only. It beats instruction-only 'ignore irrelevant' prompts.
numbers: LLaMA-2-70B-chat. GSM-IC (100 problems): in-topic distractors baseline 51.7 -> S2A 61.3 (oracle 69.7); S2A gains about 12 points with random distractors and 10 with in-topic. Instructed prompting gave no consistent gain. Opinionated TriviaQA (200 prompts): baseline 62.8% -> S2A 80.3%, oracle 82.0%.
quote: accuracy jumps up about 12% for random distractors, and 10% for in-topic distractors
limits: One model; zero-shot; costs an extra generation; figure values read from text extraction.
agent_relevance: Direct machine analogue of early selection. Candidate S1 operator: restate-and-strip before solving. Cheap to test.

source: Weston & Sukhbaatar (2023) S2A - keep-original ablation
finding: Showing the model both the cleaned and the original context loses most of the gain: the model still attends to the original distractors. The authors conclude attention must be hard, not soft.
numbers: S2A-KeepOrig 74.5% vs S2A 80.3% on opinionated TriviaQA.
limits: Single task; 200 prompts.
agent_relevance: Drop the raw context at solve time. Do not just append a cleaned copy.

source: Yoran et al. (2024) Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
finding: Retrieval can hurt. Random or low-ranked passages lower accuracy of in-context RALMs. An NLI filter prevents harm but cuts gains; fine-tuning on mixed relevant and irrelevant context does better.
numbers: Random passages drop in-context RALM accuracy by more than 10 points on average. About 1,000 training examples were enough. Fine-tuned model matched a no-retrieval model within one SD on random contexts and beat it by 3.8 (NQ) and 2.8 (2WikiMQA) points on low-ranked contexts. NLI model: BART-Large-MNLI, 407M.
limits: Fine-tuning, not scaffold; tasks NQ, 2WikiMQA, StrategyQA, Fermi, Bamboogle.
agent_relevance: An entailment gate is a code-checkable filter: only insert retrieved text that supports the question.

source: Cuconasu et al. (2024) The Power of Noise: Redefining Retrieval for RAG Systems
finding: High-scoring but non-answering documents hurt a lot, while random unrelated documents often help. Related distractors are the problem; random filler is not.
numbers: One distracting document cuts accuracy by up to 0.24 (-25%); more cut by over 0.38 (-67%) in some models. Random documents added up to the context limit raised Llama2 accuracy by up to 0.07 (+35%) with 4 retrieved documents. Noise far from the query tolerated; noise next to the query hurt.
limits: Mechanism untested (authors speculate attention conditioning). Mainly Llama2-7b and Falcon; NQ-open; Falcon did not show the gain.
agent_relevance: Matches Shi: semantic closeness drives intrusion, not volume. Place the question and key items away from task-like clutter.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Accuracy is U-shaped over the position of the relevant document: best at start or end, worst in the middle. With 20 documents, middle placement can be worse than no document at all.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo closed-book 56.1%, oracle 88.3%; performance varied by more than 20 points with position and in the worst case fell below closed-book. LongChat-13B 35.0/83.4, MPT-30B 31.5/81.9, Claude-1.3 48.3/76.1 (closed-book/oracle).
limits: Tests position and distractor quantity, not load. 2023 models; later models flatten the curve.
agent_relevance: Put task-critical content at the edges. Do not add retrieved text unless likely relevant.

source: Modarressi et al. (2025) NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching
finding: When the question shares no words with the needle, long irrelevant context hurts much more. Literal-match distractors still give cues.
numbers: GPT-4o: 99.3 base, 98.1 at 1K, 89.2 at 8K, 81.6 at 16K, 69.7 at 32K tokens. At 32K, 11 of 13 models fall below 50% of their short-context baseline. GPT-4o mini 84.8 base to 13.7 at 32K.
limits: Length and distraction are confounded.
agent_relevance: More context is a load that wears down retrieval of non-obvious links. Keep context short; keep link words visible.

source: Bianchi et al. (2025) Hidden in the Haystack: Smaller Needles Are More Difficult for LLMs to Find
finding: Short gold passages inside distractor text are found far less often, even after controlling for position and distractor volume.
numbers: Gemini-2.0-Flash 48% small gold, 62% medium, 73% large; GPT-4o 77% small to 98% large; LLaMA-3.1-405B 74% to 92%. Gemini small gold at start 94% vs 33% near the end (61-point drop); large gold 84% to 65%. 11 LLMs, over 150K runs, 3 benchmarks.
limits: Gold size, not a load manipulation.
agent_relevance: A one-line lesson in a large prompt is the likeliest item to be missed. Isolate or repeat short critical items.

source: Yang et al. (2025) How Is LLM Reasoning Distracted by Irrelevant Context? (GSM-DC)
finding: Synthetic dependency-graph benchmark with 1 to 15 injected distractors. Accuracy falls with distractor count and falls faster at greater reasoning depth. More task load gives more distraction, the reverse of Lavie's perceptual-load prediction.
numbers: Error follows a power law E ~ m^alpha(rs) in distractor count m. Grok-3-Beta alpha 0.11 at 2 steps to 0.49 at 5 steps. At 5 steps Grok-3-Beta step accuracy 43% (1 distractor) to 19% (15); GPT-4.1 26% to 2%. Training with strong distractors improved in-distribution and OOD results. Process-reward tree search added up to 6.29% OOD.
limits: Synthetic symbolic problems; load is reasoning depth (a working-memory type of load), not perceptual load. Six models.
agent_relevance: Best direct load-by-distractor grid for LLMs; it looks like working-memory load theory. In deep stages strip distractors harder, not less.

source: Gong et al. (2023) Working Memory Capacity of ChatGPT: An Empirical Study (n-back)
finding: On verbal and spatial n-back, ChatGPT accuracy falls as n rises from 1 to 3, like humans. Adding noise symbols that must be ignored significantly reduces its working-memory capacity.
numbers: Capacity about 3 in non-noise verbal variants (d' falls to about 1 at n=3). Noise variant lower. Spatial variants lower than verbal; CoT improved spatial performance significantly.
limits: GPT-3.5 only; GPT-4 not tested for cost; results in figures.
agent_relevance: Distractors shrink usable model capacity; written reasoning partly offsets. Keep working sets small, externalise state.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Thread of Thought Unraveling Chaotic Contexts
finding: A prompt that walks the context section by section, summarising relevance, then answers, beats vanilla and CoT prompts on chaotic (distractor-heavy) retrieval context.
numbers: PopQA with retrieval: ThoT best for all three models; scores 0.651 (GPT-4), 0.674 (GPT-3.5-turbo), 0.663 (LLaMA-2-70B). Prompt sweep: best templates exceed EM 0.50; very detailed instructions scored lower.
limits: Baseline numbers not fully extracted; text calls gains significant; scores quoted as in the paper text.
agent_relevance: Cheap scaffold, a cousin of S2A. Test as an S1 move.

source: Shin (2026) The inattentional gap in task conditioned AI models that omit otherwise reportable safety critical signals
finding: Narrow task instructions suppress reporting of a co-present safety-critical item that the same model reports when asked openly. A machine analogue of inattentional blindness.
numbers: Radiology text, 4 models, focused instruction: report rates 0.09 (gpt-4o-mini), 0.08 (gpt-4o), 0.48 (sonnet), 0.53 (haiku) vs about 1.00 open. Strict exclusive instruction: 0.00 for every model (N=64). Vision counting task, star: 0.00 (gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini), 0.50 haiku, 0.54 sonnet vs 0.79 to 0.96 open. Seven models overall. In a 24-scenario probe an independent open-ended critic restored every omitted finding.
limits: Single-author preprint, not peer reviewed; two duplicated scenes and two non-radiograph images disclosed; LLM judges (kappa 0.895 and 0.918).
agent_relevance: Tight task prompts make the agent miss unrequested findings. Pair each narrow solve with an open-ended side check run by code.

source: Shin (2026) Inattentional gap - Study 3, output scope
finding: Suppression is a threshold on output scope, not a smooth load gradient. One narrow sub-question switched suppression on; more sub-questions let some models recover.
numbers: Critical-finding report 1.00 at zero sub-questions, near zero at one. haiku 0.00 to 0.88 across one to three questions; OpenAI models stayed 0. Mean output length 189 characters (one question), 435, 1,046 vs 1,770 open. Model family tracked the gap more than scale: gpt-4o 0.08 vs gpt-4o-mini 0.09.
limits: Contradicts a clean Lavie-style load gradient; preprint; small item counts.
agent_relevance: Wide output scope re-admits side findings. Add an 'anything else notable' field to output schemas.

source: Hung et al. (2024) Attention Tracker: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs
finding: A prompt injection behaves like a capturing distractor: specific attention heads shift focus from the original instruction to the injected one (the distraction effect). Tracking that shift detects attacks without extra inference.
numbers: AUROC improvement of up to 10.0% over existing detection methods on Open-Prompt-Injection and deepset; works on small LLMs; training-free.
limits: Detection of injected instructions only; needs open weights.
agent_relevance: A code-side capture signal. Possible intrusion detector where attention is accessible; not for API-only models.

source: Ye et al. (2025) Differential Transformer
finding: Standard transformers give weight to irrelevant context ('attention noise') that drowns the answer. Subtracting two softmax maps cancels common-mode noise and sparsifies attention.
numbers: Matches baseline loss with about 65% of parameters or training tokens. Multi-needle retrieval at 4K: at N=6, R=2 the accuracy gap to the transformer reaches 30 points; at 64K it declines more slowly.
limits: Architecture change, 3B-scale experiments; not available to a prompt-only agent.
agent_relevance: Mechanism for S1 intrusion is a shared softmax budget, a limited-capacity view. Explains why shrinking the context helps.

source: Xu et al. (2023/24) Cognitive Overload: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with Overloaded Logical Thinking
finding: Overloading the model with multilingual, veiled-expression or effect-to-cause tasks bypasses safety behaviour in black-box attacks on Llama 2 and ChatGPT, motivated by cognitive load theory.
numbers: Tested on AdvBench and MasterKey with Llama2-7b/13b-chat, MPT and ChatGPT in many languages. Exact attack success rates were not extracted this session.
limits: Numbers not read (figures only). Load is a framing here; no load-controlled design.
agent_relevance: Heavy load may weaken the model's own rule-following. Guardrails G1-G12 should be enforced by code, not by the model, in heavy stages.

source: Struppek et al. (2025) Focused Chain-of-Thought: Efficient LLM Reasoning via Structured Input Information
finding: Training-free two-stage scaffold: extract essential facts into a short structured context, then reason only over that. Cuts tokens with comparable accuracy.
numbers: Arithmetic word problems: tokens reduced 2x to 3x with accuracy comparable to zero-shot CoT. Example: 87 output tokens vs 1,297 for traditional CoT; Qwen3 14B 43% fewer tokens in another example. Extraction by the model or by GPT-5 mini.
limits: Arithmetic only; the gain is efficiency, not accuracy.
agent_relevance: Implemented extract-then-reason loop, like early selection. Pattern for S1.

source: Xiao et al. (2024) Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
finding: Models place unused attention on the first tokens (sinks). Keeping a few sink tokens plus a recent window keeps long-stream behaviour stable.
numbers: Up to 22.2x speedup over sliding-window recomputation (abstract); only skimmed.
limits: Only skimmed; link to distractors indirect.
agent_relevance: Attention is a fixed budget that spills over, so context hygiene matters.

source: Gong et al. (2023) - CoT effect in spatial n-back
finding: Chain-of-thought significantly improved spatial n-back performance, but capacity stayed below the verbal tasks.
numbers: Abstract-reasoning variants lower still than base.
limits: GPT-3.5 only.
agent_relevance: Written reasoning acts as outside working memory; reserve it for hard depth.

source: Reading across Shi et al. (2023) and Yang et al. (2025)
finding: Two opened papers together: GSM-IC says similarity to the task drives distraction; GSM-DC says distractor count and reasoning depth raise it. Neither supports 'harder task, fewer distractor effects'.
numbers: GSM-IC macro in-topic 10.2 vs off-topic 33.0 (COT); GSM-DC alpha 0.11 to 0.49 from 2 to 5 steps.
limits: Our synthesis; different benchmarks, models and years.
agent_relevance: Filter hardest when the task is deep and surrounded by task-like material.

source: Lavie (1995, 2005) human perceptual load theory (background, not opened)
finding: Human theory the LLM tests are measured against: high perceptual load reduces distractor interference; high working-memory load increases it.
numbers: Not read this session; no human numbers quoted.
limits: Human evidence belongs to angles A and B.
agent_relevance: LLM results so far resemble the working-memory side. No LLM study found that tests the perceptual side directly.

source: Search gap: no LLM study found that manipulates perceptual load as Lavie does
finding: An arXiv search for 'perceptual load' with language model returned no results. Web search and API quotas were exhausted, so coverage comes from arXiv listing pages and direct PDFs.
numbers: 0 results for that query on 2026-11-01.
limits: Coverage limited; unopened candidates: arXiv 2603.00270 (Dual-Process Interference), 2601.11585 (Entropic Context Shaping).
agent_relevance: Treat LLM perceptual-load as open. Use our own distractor-by-difficulty grid.

source: Modarressi et al. (2025) NoLiMa - effective context length
finding: Claimed context size is far above the length at which accuracy holds up. Effective length is where score stays above 85% of the model base score.
numbers: GPT-4o claimed 128K, effective 8K. GPT-4o mini claimed 128K, effective under 1K. Threshold set at 85% of each model base score (GPT-4o base 99.3, threshold 84.4).
limits: Threshold choice is the authors; needle style task.
agent_relevance: Budget real working context well below advertised limits; load grows quickly with length.
